title: Arbitrary coproducts of distinguished triangles
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a pre-triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] and $I$ a set. Let $T_i=(X_i\to Y_i\to Z_i\to X_i[1])$ be distinguished triangles. Assume that the coproducts of the three vertex families and of $(X_i[1])_i$ exist. Then the componentwise coproduct triangle, with its last arrow composed with the canonical comparison $\bigoplus_i X_i[1]\cong(\bigoplus_i X_i)[1]$, is distinguished. The index set may be empty.

proof.text: The shift is an equivalence and hence preserves every existing coproduct. The canonical coproduct comparison on shifted first vertices is therefore invertible.

Complete the coproduct of the first arrows to a distinguished triangle. TR3 gives maps from the summand triangles into this triangle, and the coproduct universal property assembles a morphism from the componentwise coproduct triangle to it, identical on the first two vertices. For every object A, applying Hom(-,A) to the coproduct triangle gives the product of the summand exact Hom sequences; this sequence is exact since products of exact sequences of abelian groups are exact. Comparing with the distinguished triangle, the five lemma makes the map on third vertices bijective on Hom(-,A). Yoneda makes it an isomorphism, and TR1 shows the coproduct triangle distinguished. Equivalently this is the dual of the product proof in the cited Stacks lemma. This is already fully proved by the attached source-library declaration; no new Lean assertion is introduced.
